4.5
Eigenspace of
\hat{C}_{2}
of dimension 8: sector of the
35

Four irreps have
C_{R}=3N+3
, namely,
{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}
,
{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}
,
{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}
,
{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}
(see Table
2
), which can be grouped into two pairs of irreps linked by complex conjugation,
\{{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+},{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}\}
and
\{{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-},{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}\}
, or into two pairs of equivalent irreps,
\{{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+},{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}\}
and
\{{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+},{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}\}
. In the full color space of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, the
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenspace of eigenvalue
3N+3
is thus of dimension 8, spanned by four projectors (
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}$}}
) and four transition operators (
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}
). These operators can be easily found using a combination of the procedures seen previously in sections
4.3
and
4.4
.

For instance, the kernel of the operator (
109
) for
C_{R}=3N+3
and
(s_{12},s_{34})=(+,+)
directly gives two
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenvectors which must be linear combinations of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}
and
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}
.
Projecting these eigenvectors using
\frac{{\mathds{1}}\pm\sigma_{\rm cc}}{2}
to make them either even or odd under complex conjugation, we get two eigenvectors
e_{1}\propto{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}+{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}
and
e_{2}\propto{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}-{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}
. Of course,
e_{1}
and
e_{2}
can be obtained in a single operation by searching for the kernel of the operator

\displaystyle\frac{{\mathds{1}}+s_{12}\sigma_{12}}{2}\cdot\frac{{\mathds{1}}+s_{34}\sigma_{34}}{2}\cdot\frac{{\mathds{1}}+\lambda_{\rm cc}\sigma_{\rm cc}}{2}\cdot\hat{C}_{2}-C_{R}\,{\mathds{1}}\ ,

(135)

for
C_{R}=3N+3
and setting
(s_{12},s_{34},\lambda_{\rm cc})=(+,+,+)
and
(+,+,-)
, respectively.

Then, the specific linear combinations
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}/{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}\propto e_{1}\pm\lambda e_{2}
are obtained as in section
4.3
, by observing that the irrep
35
is characterized by three symmetrized quark indices, see (
34
).
Symmetrizing the three-quark intermediate state of any of the tensors
J_{1}\ldots J_{8}
and
K_{1}\ldots K_{8}
(corresponding to the class of tensors with ‘one trace’, see Table
3
, containing the leading tensors of the irrep
35
) should thus leave the expression of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}
unchanged.
When inserting in
J_{1}
the three-quark symmetrizer (
124
), we have
J_{1}\rightarrow\frac{1}{3}(J_{1}+2J_{3})
.
Thus,
J_{1}
can enter the expression of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}
only via the latter linear combination, and this information suffices to determine the parameter
\lambda
in
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}/{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}\propto e_{1}\pm\lambda e_{2}
. Finally, the normalization of projectors is fixed as usual.

Using the same procedure for
(s_{12},s_{34},\lambda_{\rm cc})=(-,-,\pm)
,
(+,-,\pm)
and
(-,+,\pm)
, we obtain the expressions of
\{{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}$}}\}
,
\{{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}$}}\}
and
\{{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}\}
, respectively. Note that since the transition operators involving the
35
(i.e.
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}$}}
and
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}
) are built from
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}
and
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}$}}
(see (
60
)), they have the same symmetries in quark/antiquark indices, and must also depend on the combination
J_{1}+2J_{3}
.

The eight operators sought are as follows:

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}/{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}

\displaystyle=\ \frac{2(N+2)}{9(N+1)(N+3)}\left\{\phantom{\frac{1}{1}}\hskip-5.69054pt2(J_{12}+K_{12})-4(J_{78}+K_{78})+J_{34}+J_{56}+K_{34}+K_{56}\right.

\displaystyle\hskip-34.1433pt\left.-\frac{2(C_{12}+C_{34})-8(Z_{12}+Z_{34})+8(H_{12}+H_{34})}{N+1}\ \pm 3(J_{34}-J_{56}+K_{34}-K_{56})\phantom{\frac{1}{1}}\hskip-5.69054pt\right\}

(136)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}/{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}$}}

\displaystyle=\ \frac{2(N+2)}{9(N-1)(N+5)}\left\{\phantom{\frac{1}{1}}\hskip-5.69054pt2(J_{12}-K_{12})-4(J_{78}-K_{78})+J_{34}+J_{56}-K_{34}-K_{56}\right.

\displaystyle\hskip-34.1433pt\left.-\frac{2(C_{12}-C_{34})}{N+1}-\frac{24{\overline{H}}_{12}}{N+3}+\frac{16(B_{12}-B_{34})}{(N+1)(N+3)}\ \pm 3\left(J_{34}-J_{56}-K_{34}+K_{56}+\frac{8{\overline{H}}_{34}}{N+3}\right)\right\}

\displaystyle{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}/{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}_{+}$}}=

\displaystyle\ 2{\overline{J}}_{12}-4{\overline{J}}_{78}+J_{35}-J_{46}+3(J_{36}-J_{45})-\frac{2{\overline{C}}_{12}-4Z_{13}+4Z_{24}}{N+1}

\displaystyle\hskip-85.35826pt\pm\left(-2{\overline{K}}_{12}+4{\overline{K}}_{78}-K_{35}+K_{46}-3(K_{36}-K_{45})+\frac{2{\overline{C}}_{34}-4Z_{14}+4Z_{23}}{N+1}\right)

(138a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}/{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{35}$}}_{+}$}}=

\displaystyle\ -2{\overline{J}}_{12}+4{\overline{J}}_{78}-J_{35}+J_{46}+3(J_{36}-J_{45})+\frac{2{\overline{C}}_{12}-4Z_{13}+4Z_{24}}{N+1}

\displaystyle\hskip-85.35826pt\pm\left(2{\overline{K}}_{12}-4{\overline{K}}_{78}+K_{35}-K_{46}-3(K_{36}-K_{45})-\frac{2{\overline{C}}_{34}-4Z_{14}+4Z_{23}}{N+1}\right)

(138b)

Normalizing transition operators as in (
85
) can be done as in sections
4.4.2
and
4.4.3
for the sectors of the
{\mbox{\boldmath$0$}}_{b}
and of the
64
. Replacing
{\mbox{\boldmath$0$}}_{b}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$35$}}
in (
121
) and in (
122
), one gets the two vertices
v_{1}
and
v_{2}
and the expression of
v_{1}^{\dagger}v_{1}
.
The projector on the irrep
35
of
qqq\bar{q}\bar{q}\bar{q}
is of the form (
126
), with the quark (resp. antiquark) sub-system in the irrep
10
(resp.
8
) of projector given by (
124
) (resp. by the conjugate of (
125
)). We obtain:

\displaystyle v_{1}^{\dagger}v_{1}\

\displaystyle=\ \frac{2}{9}\left\{J_{1}-J_{5}+2J_{3}-2J_{7}\right\}\ +\ \ldots

(139)

Comparing (
136
)-(
136
) with (
115
) we get:

\displaystyle a=\sqrt{\frac{2(N+2)}{(N+1)(N+3)}}\ \ ;\ \ b=\sqrt{\frac{2(N+2)}{(N-1)(N+5)}}\ ,

(140)

and the expressions (
138
) should be multiplied by
\frac{1}{9}ab
to satisfy the normalization (

).

4.6
Eigenspace of
\hat{C}_{2}
of dimension 9: sector of the
27

We will now consider the eigenspace of
\hat{C}_{2}
associated to the eigenvalue
C_{R}=2N+2
(the Casimir of the irrep
27
, see Table
2
). Since the
27
appears three times in the decomposition of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, this eigenspace, denoted by
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
and dubbed as the ‘sector of the
27
’, is of dimension 9: it is spanned by three projectors (
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}
,
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
,
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
) and six transition operators (
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
,
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
,
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
and their Hermitian conjugates).

The projector
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}
can be obtained directly from the kernel of the operator (
109
) for
C_{R}=2N+2
and
(s_{12},s_{34})=(-,-)
, and using Appendix
B.3
to fix the normalization
\mathrm{Tr}\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}={K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
. One finds

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}=\frac{(N+2)}{(N-2)(N+1)(N+4)}\left\{C_{12}-C_{34}-\frac{4\left(B_{12}-B_{34}\right)}{N+2}\right\}\ .

(141)

However, the method used in the previous sections proves insufficient to find the two other projectors and the six transition operators in
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
. For instance, in order to look for the Hermitian projectors
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
, one may consider the kernel of
16
16

16

Recall that
\sigma_{\rm hc}
denotes the Hermitian conjugation operator.

\frac{{\mathds{1}}+s_{12}\sigma_{12}}{2}\cdot\frac{{\mathds{1}}+s_{34}\sigma_{34}}{2}\cdot\frac{{\mathds{1}}+\lambda_{\rm hc}\sigma_{\rm hc}}{2}\cdot\hat{C}_{2}-C_{R}\,{\mathds{1}}\ \

(142)

for
(s_{12},s_{34},\lambda_{\rm hc})=(+,+,+)
. But this subspace of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
is of dimension 3. It is spanned by
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
,
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
, and the sum of transition operators
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}+{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
, and it is not possible to further separate this subspace using symmetry arguments.
Due to the presence of three equivalent irreps
27
, two of which have a fortiori the same symmetry with respect to the permutation
\sigma_{12}
(namely
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}
and
{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}
), the sector of the
27
is a little more complex than the other eigenspaces of
\hat{C}_{2}
considered previously.

To determine the projectors
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
, as well as the six transition operators, we first need to derive the multiplication table between the tensors of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
.

4.6.1
Vertices for
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}

From the knowledge of
\hat{C}_{2}
, we can directly write nine eigenvectors of
\hat{C}_{2}
associated to the eigenvalue
C_{R}=2N+2
, i.e., a basis of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
:

\displaystyle\tilde{H}\equiv

\displaystyle\ \frac{H_{12}+H_{34}}{4}-\frac{B_{12}+B_{34}}{4(N+2)}+\frac{S}{2(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(143a)

\displaystyle\tilde{Z}_{1}\equiv

\displaystyle\ Z_{1}-\frac{B_{13}}{N+2}+\frac{S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(143b)

\displaystyle\tilde{Z}_{2}\equiv

\displaystyle\ Z_{2}-\frac{B_{24}}{N+2}+\frac{S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(143c)

\displaystyle\tilde{Z}_{3}\equiv

\displaystyle\ Z_{3}-\frac{B_{14}}{N+2}+\frac{S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(143d)

\displaystyle\tilde{Z}_{4}\equiv

\displaystyle\ Z_{4}-\frac{B_{23}}{N+2}+\frac{S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(143e)

\displaystyle\tilde{C}_{i}\equiv

\displaystyle\ C_{i}-\frac{4B_{i}}{N+2}+\frac{2\,S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\hskip 14.22636pt({\rm for}\ i=1,\ldots,4)\ .

(143f)

From the birdtrack expressions of the tensors given in Table
3
, we see that in each of the above expressions, the ‘leading term’ (involving the tensors associated to the lowest number of traces) corresponds to an intermediate state made of a symmetric quark pair and a symmetric antiquark pair, whose decomposition into irreps is given by (
3
)–(
4
). Subtracting the irreps
1
and
8
from this leading term (i.e., replacing the intermediate state by the projector (
5
)) directly yields each of the expressions (
143
). This shows that the nine eigenvectors (
143
) can be represented pictorially as the birdtrack for the leading term, up to the replacement of the intermediate state by the blob denoting the projector (
5
) on the irrep
27
. For instance:

(145)

and renaming the eigenvectors (

) as

\displaystyle\{\tilde{H},\tilde{Z}_{1},\tilde{Z}_{2},\tilde{Z}_{3},\tilde{Z}_{4},\tilde{C}_{1},\tilde{C}_{2},\tilde{C}_{3},\tilde{C}_{4}\}\equiv\{E_{11},E_{12},E_{13},E_{21},E_{31},E_{22},E_{33},E_{32},E_{23}\}\ ,

(146)

we quickly verify
visually
that the nine eigenvectors are related to the
v_{i}
’s as follows:
17
17

17

Recall that in the product
v_{i}^{\dagger}v_{j}
, the operator
v_{j}
applies first and is drawn to the left in the corresponding birdtrack expression, see footnote
11
.

\displaystyle E_{ij}\ =\ v_{i}^{\dagger}v_{j}\ .

(147)

In the following we will need the traces of the
E_{ij}
’s, which using (
146
) and (
143
) are directly obtained from the traces of the tensors
\tau
listed in Appendix
B.3
.
Since those traces are real, we can write
\mathrm{Tr}\,(E_{ij})=\mathrm{Tr}\,(v_{i}^{\dagger}v_{j})=\mathrm{Tr}\,(v_{j}^{\dagger}v_{i})=\mathrm{Tr}\,(E_{ji})
, so that

\displaystyle n_{ij}\equiv\frac{\mathrm{Tr}\,(E_{ij})}{{K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}}

(148)

is a real, symmetric
3\times 3
matrix. We find:

\displaystyle n_{11}=

\displaystyle\ \frac{N^{5}+9N^{4}+23N^{3}+11N^{2}+8N+28}{16(N+1)(N+2)^{2}}\ ,

(149a)

\displaystyle n_{22}=

\displaystyle\ n_{33}=\ \frac{N^{5}+6N^{4}+5N^{3}-20N^{2}-20N+8}{2(N+1)(N+2)^{2}}\ ,

(149b)

\displaystyle n_{12}=

\displaystyle\ n_{13}=\ -\frac{(2N+3)\left(N^{2}+3N-2\right)}{2(N+1)(N+2)^{2}}\ ,

(149c)

\displaystyle n_{23}=

\displaystyle\ \frac{4(2N+3)}{(N+1)(N+2)^{2}}\ .

(149d)

The multiplication table of the eigenvectors (
146
) then reads

\displaystyle E_{ij}E_{kl}\ =

\displaystyle\ v_{i}^{\dagger}v_{j}v_{k}^{\dagger}v_{l}=n_{jk}v_{i}^{\dagger}v_{l}=n_{jk}E_{il}\ ,

(150)

where we used
v_{j}v_{k}^{\dagger}=\frac{1}{{K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}}\,\mathrm{Tr}\,(v_{j}v_{k}^{\dagger})\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
(a direct consequence of Schur’s lemma, with
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
defined by (
5
)), and
\mathrm{Tr}\,(v_{j}v_{k}^{\dagger})=\mathrm{Tr}\,(v_{k}^{\dagger}v_{j})={K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}\,n_{jk}\,
.

4.6.2
Projectors and transition operators of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}

In this section we derive the three projectors and six transition operators of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
, starting from their general expression in terms of the vertices (
145
).

Under
\psi\leftrightarrow\chi
,
v_{1}
is invariant and
v_{2}\leftrightarrow v_{3}
. From the symmetries of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}
,
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}
and
{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}
under
\psi\leftrightarrow\chi
, the corresponding projectors must be of the form (see section
4.1
):

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}

\displaystyle=\ \left[av_{1}+b(v_{2}+v_{3})\right]^{\dagger}\left[av_{1}+b(v_{2}+v_{3})\right]\ ,

(151a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}

\displaystyle=\ \left[a^{\prime}v_{1}+b^{\prime}(v_{2}+v_{3})\right]^{\dagger}\left[a^{\prime}v_{1}+b^{\prime}(v_{2}+v_{3})\right]\ ,

(151b)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}

\displaystyle=\ \left[r(v_{2}-v_{3})\right]^{\dagger}\left[r(v_{2}-v_{3})\right]\ .

(151c)

We need to find the coefficients
a,\,b,\,a^{\prime},\,b^{\prime},\,r
ensuring that each projector indeed projects on an irrep

, and that the three projectors are orthogonal to each other.

First, the coefficient
r
in the projector
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}
is directly obtained by expanding (

),

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}

\displaystyle=\ r^{2}\left(v_{2}^{\dagger}v_{2}+v_{3}^{\dagger}v_{3}-v_{2}^{\dagger}v_{3}-v_{3}^{\dagger}v_{2}\right)\ ,

(152)

and imposing
\mathrm{Tr}\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}={K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}

(see (

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}

\displaystyle=\ c_{a}^{\dagger}c_{a}\ =\ \frac{\tilde{C}_{1}+\tilde{C}_{2}-\tilde{C}_{3}-\tilde{C}_{4}}{2(n_{22}-n_{23})}\ ,

(153)

where

\displaystyle c_{a}

\displaystyle\equiv\ \frac{v_{2}-v_{3}}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}-n_{23})}}\ .

Using (

(155)

As a non-trivial cross-check one can verify using the multiplication table (

{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}^{2}={\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}
.
The fact that

(see (

We now look for the projectors
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and

, which after some rescaling of the parameters

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}

\displaystyle=\ c_{1}^{\dagger}c_{1}\ ,

(156a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}

\displaystyle=\ c_{2}^{\dagger}c_{2}\ ,

(156b)

in terms of the ‘symmetric clebsches’

\displaystyle c_{1}

\displaystyle\equiv\ a\,\frac{v_{1}}{\sqrt{n_{11}}}+b\,\frac{v_{2}+v_{3}}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}}\ ,

(157a)

\displaystyle c_{2}

\displaystyle\equiv\ a^{\prime}\frac{v_{1}}{\sqrt{n_{11}}}+b^{\prime}\,\frac{v_{2}+v_{3}}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}}\ .

(157b)

Expanding the expressions (

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}\

\displaystyle=\ a^{2}\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}\,+b^{2}\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\,-\frac{2ab}{\sqrt{\rho}}\frac{\tilde{Z}}{4n_{12}}\ ,

(158a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}\

\displaystyle=\ a^{\prime\,2}\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}\,+b^{\prime\,2}\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\,-\frac{2a^{\prime}b^{\prime}}{\sqrt{\rho}}\frac{\tilde{Z}}{4n_{12}}\ ,

\displaystyle\ C_{12}+C_{34}-\frac{4(B_{12}+B_{34})}{N+2}+\frac{8\,S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(159a)

\displaystyle\tilde{Z}\equiv\sum_{i=1}^{4}\tilde{Z}_{i}\ =

\displaystyle\ Z_{12}+Z_{34}-\frac{2(B_{12}+B_{34})}{N+2}+\frac{4S}{(N+1)(N+2)}\ ,

(159b)

and the parameter

by

\rho>1
for any

.

\displaystyle\rho\ \equiv\ \frac{n_{11}(n_{22}+n_{23})}{2n_{12}^{2}}\ >\,1\ .

(160)

The fact that
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}

and

We now determine the coefficients
a,\,b,\,a^{\prime},\,b^{\prime}
appearing in (

) and (

). Requiring
\mathrm{Tr}\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}=\mathrm{Tr}\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}={K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
, we obtain:
20

In (

), use
\mathrm{Tr}\,\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}=\mathrm{Tr}\,\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}=\mathrm{Tr}\,\frac{\tilde{Z}}{4n_{12}}={K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}

\displaystyle a^{2}+b^{2}-\frac{2ab}{\sqrt{\rho}}\ =\ a^{\prime\,2}+b^{\prime\,2}-\frac{2a^{\prime}b^{\prime}}{\sqrt{\rho}}\ =\ 1\ .

(161)

The orthogonality of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}

\displaystyle aa^{\prime}+bb^{\prime}-\frac{a^{\prime}b+ab^{\prime}}{\sqrt{\rho}}\

Equations (

All solutions for the projectors (

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}

\displaystyle\equiv P(t)=\frac{\rho}{\rho-1}\left[\frac{\cos^{2}{(\theta+t)}}{n_{11}}\,\tilde{H}+\frac{\cos^{2}{(\theta-t)}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\,\tilde{C}\right]-\frac{1+\sqrt{\rho}\cos{2t}}{4n_{12}(\rho-1)}\,\tilde{Z}\ ,

(163a)

\displaystyle\equiv P^{\prime}(t)=\frac{\rho}{\rho-1}\left[\frac{\sin^{2}{(\theta+t)}}{n_{11}}\,\tilde{H}+\frac{\sin^{2}{(\theta-t)}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\,\tilde{C}\right]-\frac{1-\sqrt{\rho}\cos{2t}}{4n_{12}(\rho-1)}\,\tilde{Z}\ ,

where the fixed parameter

. Noting that

and

The non-unicity of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and

arises from the non-unicity of clebsches

and

cannot be distinguished from their ‘external’ symmetry under

21
21

21

A similar situation illustrating the non-unicity of projectors associated with equivalent irreps is encountered when decomposing simple systems of three partons, such as
qqq
,

,
(qg)_{{}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$15$}}$}}}{g}
, see Ref.
[

]
.

As expected from section

(see (

) and the following discussion) and checked in Appendix

(see (

)), the set of solutions for

)), the sum of projectors,

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\rm sum}$}}{}\equiv P(t)+P^{\prime}(t)\ =

\displaystyle\ \frac{\rho}{\rho-1}\left[\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}+\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\right]-\frac{1}{\rho-1}\,\frac{\tilde{Z}}{2n_{12}}\ ,

is independent of

, i.e., uniquely defined.
22
22

22

In the present study of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, this also follows trivially from the completeness relation (

), since to the exception of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and

The pair

is thus determined by giving either

or

, and since

to find all solutions. A few convenient choices for
({\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}})
, corresponding to some specific values of

, are listed in Appendix

.

We end this section by giving the expressions of the six transition operators of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
. These operators all depend on
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
or
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
, and thus on the continuous parameter

.
From section
4.1
and the expressions of
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}
(resp.
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}

) given in (

) (resp. (

) (resp. symmetric clebsches (

)), the transition operators normalized according to (

) are:

\displaystyle{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}

\displaystyle\equiv\ T(t)\ =\ c_{2}^{\dagger}c_{1}\ ,

(165a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}

\displaystyle\equiv\ T_{a}(t)\ =\ c_{a}^{\dagger}c_{1}\ ,

(165b)

\displaystyle{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}$}}

\displaystyle\equiv\ T^{\prime}_{a}(t)\ =\ c_{a}^{\dagger}c_{2}\ ,

(165c)

the other three transition operators being obtained by Hermitian conjugation.
Expanding (
165
) and using (

), (

) and (

) we obtain:

\displaystyle T(t)

\displaystyle=\ aa^{\prime}\frac{\widetilde{H}}{n_{11}}+bb^{\prime}\frac{\widetilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}-\frac{a^{\prime}b(\widetilde{Z}_{1}+\widetilde{Z}_{2})+ab^{\prime}(\widetilde{Z}_{3}+\widetilde{Z}_{4})}{2n_{12}\sqrt{\rho}}\ ,

(166a)

\displaystyle T_{a}(t)

\displaystyle=\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}-n_{23})}}\left[a\,\frac{\widetilde{Z}_{3}-\widetilde{Z}_{4}}{\sqrt{n_{11}}}+b\,\frac{\widetilde{C}_{1}+\widetilde{C}_{4}-\widetilde{C}_{2}-\widetilde{C}_{3}}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}}\right]\ ,

(166b)

\displaystyle T^{\prime}_{a}(t)

\displaystyle=\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}-n_{23})}}\left[a^{\prime}\,\frac{\widetilde{Z}_{3}-\widetilde{Z}_{4}}{\sqrt{n_{11}}}+b^{\prime}\,\frac{\widetilde{C}_{1}+\widetilde{C}_{4}-\widetilde{C}_{2}-\widetilde{C}_{3}}{\sqrt{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}}\right]\ .

(166c)

With
a,b,a^{\prime},b^{\prime}
given by (

), the ‘tilde tensors’ defined by (

), and the Hermitian conjugates being obtained using Table

, the expressions (

in explicit form, for any choice of the parameter

.

In the next section we will choose a value of
t
to define
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}=P(t)
,
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}=P^{\prime}(t)
and the six transition operators (
T(t),\,T_{a}(t),\,T^{\prime}_{a}(t)
and their Hermitian conjugates), this set of eight operators being defined in terms of clebsches by (
156
) and (
165
). In case we want to make another choice, the relation between sets corresponding to different values of
t
directly follows from the symmetric clebsches transforming under a simple rotation
R(t)\in{\rm SO}(2)
when

changes, see (
200b
)-(
201
).

Consider first the subset
\{P(t),\,P^{\prime}(t),\,T(t),\,T(t)^{\dagger}\}
. According to (
90b
), the
matrix of operators (
86
) for a general parameter

is related to that for

by

\displaystyle\left(\begin{matrix}P(t)\ &\ T(t)^{\dagger}\ \\[5.69054pt]
T(t)\ &\ P^{\prime}(t)\end{matrix}\right)\ =\ R(t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}P(0)\ &\ T(0)^{\dagger}\ \\[5.69054pt]
T(0)\ &\ P^{\prime}(0)\end{matrix}\right)\cdot R(t)^{\intercal}\ .

(167)

Using (
200b
) and performing the matrix product in (
167
), we find

\displaystyle P(t)+P^{\prime}(t)

\displaystyle=\ P(0)+P^{\prime}(0)\ ,

(168a)

\displaystyle T(t)-T(t)^{\dagger}

\displaystyle=\ T(0)-T(0)^{\dagger}\ ,

(168b)

\displaystyle\left(\begin{matrix}P(t)-P^{\prime}(t)\\[5.69054pt]
T(t)+T^{\dagger}(t)\end{matrix}\right)=\

\displaystyle R(2t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}P(0)-P^{\prime}(0)\\[5.69054pt]
T(0)+T(0)^{\dagger}\end{matrix}\right)\ .

(168c)

We see that not only
P+P^{\prime}
, but also the linear combination
T-T^{\dagger}
is independent of
t
,
23
23

23

The difference of the off-diagonal elements of a
2\times 2
matrix is indeed invariant under a similarity transformation when the latter is a rotation, as in (
167
). But the unicity of
T-T^{\dagger}
can also be understood as follows. In the subspace of
{\cal E}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}
being symmetric under
\sigma_{12}
and
\sigma_{34}
, of basis
\{P(t),P^{\prime}(t),T(t),T(t)^{\dagger}\}
, the operator

is the only possible

) being one-dimensional for
(s_{12},s_{34},\lambda_{\rm hc})=(+,+,-)
. Non-unicity only appears in the sector of Hermitian tensors – the kernel of (
142
) for
(s_{12},s_{34},\lambda_{\rm hc})=(+,+,+)
, of basis
\{P(t),P^{\prime}(t),T(t)+T(t)^{\dagger}\}
.
Note also that

is the ‘square root’ of
P+P^{\prime}
, which simply follows from (
85

\displaystyle(T-T^{\dagger})^{2}

\displaystyle=-(P+P^{\prime})\ .

and that the doublet
(P-P^{\prime},T+T^{\dagger})
transforms under a rotation of parameter
2t
when
t
varies.
As a cross-check, we easily verify that the general expressions (
163
) and (
166a
) found for
P(t)
,
P^{\prime}(t)
and

indeed satisfy (

) and (

As for the subset
\{T_{a}(t),\,T^{\prime}_{a}(t),T_{a}(t)^{\dagger},\,T^{\prime}_{a}(t)^{\dagger}\}
, we directly find using (

)-(

) and (

transform like the doublet of symmetric clebsches

when

\displaystyle\left(\begin{matrix}T_{a}(t)\\[5.69054pt]
T^{\prime}_{a}(t)\end{matrix}\right)=c_{a}^{\dagger}\left(\begin{matrix}c_{1}(t)\\[5.69054pt]
c_{2}(t)\end{matrix}\right)=R(t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}T_{a}(0)\\[5.69054pt]
T^{\prime}_{a}(0)\end{matrix}\right);\ \left(\begin{matrix}T_{a}(t)^{\dagger}\\[5.69054pt]
T^{\prime}_{a}(t)^{\dagger}\end{matrix}\right)=\left(\begin{matrix}c_{1}(t)^{\dagger}\\[5.69054pt]
c_{2}(t)^{\dagger}\end{matrix}\right)c_{a}=R(t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}T_{a}(0)^{\dagger}\\[5.69054pt]
T^{\prime}_{a}(0)^{\dagger}\end{matrix}\right)\ .

It follows that any linear combination of the doublets
(T_{a}(t),\,T^{\prime}_{a}(t))
and
(T_{a}(t)^{\dagger},\,T^{\prime}_{a}(t)^{\dagger})
will transform in the same way under a change of parameter

.

5
Soft anomalous dimension matrix

A rigorous treatment of hard QCD processes requires including corrections from induced gluon radiation. Soft and quasi-collinear gluon radiation gives rise to double logarithmic (DL) contributions, resummed in (exponential) Sudakov form factors, one for each of the external partons (the Sudakov factor associated to a given parton depending on
N
only through the color charge of that parton). For hard processes where the external particles comprise only two or three partons (with possibly other electroweak particles), it is possible, thanks to the
color triviality

[
14
]
of such processes, to account for both DL and SL corrections by a product of Sudakov form factors. However, already for processes involving four partons, certain SL contributions from soft and large-angle gluon radiation cannot be taken into account in this way
[
8
]
, and require the introduction of a “fifth form factor”
[
14
]
, obtained by exponentiating the so-called soft anomalous dimension matrix (sADM)
[
8
,
9
,
10
,
11
,
12
,
13
,
14
]
.

The sADM associated with a
2\to 2
partonic process depends on the different color states available in the
s,t,u
channels of the process, and therefore presents a
non-trivial
color structure, requiring knowledge of the Hermitian projectors on the two-parton states (and in general of transition operators between them) in the different channels. In this section we consider the sADM of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, defined in the
s
-channel as

5.1
Quantum numbers and crossing symmetry

The (
s
-channel) quadratic Casimir operator
\hat{C}_{2}
and the operators
\sigma_{\rm cc}
,
\sigma_{y}\equiv\sigma_{14}\sigma_{23}
,
\sigma_{x}\equiv\sigma_{12}\sigma_{34}
are diagonalizable and commute.

24

\{{\mathds{1}},\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}\}

{\rm S}_{4}
). This motivates the notations
\sigma_{x}
and
\sigma_{y}
for the reflections in the horizontal and vertical axes.

and are explicitly known from the expressions of all (
s

The forms (
5.1
) of the matrices
K_{ts}
and
K_{us}
are useful for visualizing how sets with different quantum numbers are matched when moving from the
\mathcal{V}^{(s)}
basis to the
\mathcal{V}^{(t)}
or
\mathcal{V}^{(u)}
basis, and also for deducing the general structure of the sADM (see next section).

5.2
Structure of the sADM

The sADM associated to the
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
process is obtained from the operator
\mathcal{Q}
defined as
[
14
]
:

\displaystyle\mathcal{Q}(b)\ =\ \frac{1+b}{2N}\,T_{t}^{2}+\frac{1-b}{2N}\,T_{u}^{2}\ ,

(180)

where
b
is a kinematic variable depending on the Mandelstam variables
s,t,u
of the
2\to 2
process,
29
29

29

Namely,
b=\frac{T-U}{T+U}
where
T=\ln\frac{s}{-t}-i\pi
and
U=\ln\frac{s}{-u}-i\pi

[
14
]
.
and
T_{t}^{2}\equiv\hat{C}_{2}^{(t)}
(resp.
T_{u}^{2}\equiv\hat{C}_{2}^{(u)}
) is the
t
-channel (resp.
u
-channel),
{\rm SU}(N)
invariant Casimir operator (defined below in terms of birdtracks).

The elements of the
t
-channel basis
\mathcal{V}^{(t)}
are eigenvectors of
T_{t}^{2}
, ordered as for the
s
-channel (second column of Table
1
). In the
t
-channel basis, the operator
T_{t}^{2}
is thus simply represented by the diagonal matrix
\mathcal{C}
of the corresponding Casimirs. In the
u
-channel basis
\mathcal{V}^{(u)}
, the operator
T_{u}^{2}
is obviously represented by the same matrix
\mathcal{C}
. Using the
K_{ts}
and
K_{us}
transition matrices defined by (
178
), the matrix
\mathcal{Q}^{(s)}
of the operator
\mathcal{Q}
in the
s
-channel basis
\mathcal{V}^{(s)}
thus reads:

\displaystyle\mathcal{Q}^{(s)}(b)\

\displaystyle=\ \frac{1+b}{2N}\,K_{ts}\cdot{\cal C}\cdot K_{ts}+\frac{1-b}{2N}\,K_{us}\cdot{\cal C}\cdot K_{us}\ .

(181)

From the general form (
5.1
) of
K_{ts}
and
K_{us}
, it follows directly that
\mathcal{Q}^{(s)}
is block-diagonal, with blocks of size
(21,1,1,1,6,6,6)
(similarly to the matrix
G^{\prime}
, see (
176
)). Thus, each subspace with given quantum numbers
\lambda
is invariant under the action of the sADM.

It is interesting to prove this last result in a basis-independent way. To this end, it is convenient to represent operators acting on the color space of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
(such as the
s
-channel Casimir operator
\hat{C}_{2}
acting on the basis
{\cal T}
of tensors, see (
63
)) as operators acting on the space
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}^{\otimes 4}
of all color singlet states which can be built from four
27
’s. In birdtrack notation, a basis of this space is simply obtained from the basis
\mathcal{T}
(given in Table
3
) by stretching the external “parton legs” of a given tensor
\tau
to the same side, and thus build vectors in a “bra/ket” notation. For example, the tensor
{B_{1}}
(a linear map
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\rightarrow{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
) is traded for the ket
|{B_{1}}\rangle
(a singlet state of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}^{\otimes 4}
) according to:

\lxSVG@closescope }}}

We recall that the generalized partons
\psi_{1}
,
\chi_{2}
,
\chi_{3}
,
\psi_{4}
belong to the irrep
27
, as specified by the abbreviated notation (
62
). Note that since the irrep
27
is self-conjugate, in the birdtrack for the ket
|{B_{1}}\rangle
we could write
\bar{\chi}_{3}=\chi_{3}
and
\bar{\psi}_{4}=\psi_{4}
.

With the above pictorial notations, an operator acting on kets can be viewed as a map

\psi_{1}\chi_{2}\bar{\chi}_{3}\bar{\psi}_{4}\to\psi_{1}^{\prime}\chi_{2}^{\prime}\bar{\chi}_{3}^{\prime}\bar{\psi}_{4}^{\prime}
. For instance, the inner product in the space of kets,
\langle\tau_{i}|\tau_{j}\rangle=\langle\tau_{i}|{\mathds{1}}|\tau_{j}\rangle
, involves the identity operator

(186b)

In summary,
T_{t}^{2}
and
T_{u}^{2}
are invariant under the action of the operators
\{\sigma_{\rm cc},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{x}\}
defining quantum numbers, and so is the operator
\mathcal{Q}
. The simplicity of the proof makes obvious the
(21,1,1,1,6,6,6)
block-diagonal structure of the sADM (i.e., the matrix representation of
\mathcal{Q}
) found in the basis
\mathcal{V}^{(s)}
(see (
181
)).

5.3
Characteristic polynomial

As a consequence of section
5.2
, the sADM characteristic polynomial factorizes as a product of seven factors, each factor being the characteristic polynomial of the block defining the sADM restricted to the subspace
\mathcal{V}_{\lambda}^{(s)}
of quantum numbers
\lambda
. Namely,

\displaystyle{\rm Det}\left(x\,{\mathds{1}}-\mathcal{Q}^{(s)}(b)\right)\ =\ \prod_{\lambda}\ f_{\lambda}(x,b)\ ,

(187)

where the polynomials
f_{\lambda}(x,b)
, ordered according to their quantum number label
\lambda
as in Table
1
(first column), are of degree
21,\,1,\,1,\,1,\,6,\,6,\,6
, respectively.

The explicit calculation shows that each factor
f_{\lambda}(x,b)
of degree
>1
can actually be factorized into polynomials of smaller degree. We obtain:

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(+,+,+)}}(x,b)\ =\ (x-r_{1})(x-r_{2})(x-r_{3})p_{1}(x,b)p_{2}(x,b)p_{2}(x,-b)p_{3}(x,b)

(188a)

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(+,+,-)}}(x,b)\ =\ x-r_{1}

(188b)

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(+,-,+)}}(x,b)\ =\ x-r_{2}

(188c)

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(+,-,-)}}(x,b)\ =\ x-r_{3}

(188d)

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(-,+,-)}}(x,b)\ =\ (x-r_{2})(x-r_{3})p_{2}(x,b)

(188e)

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(-,-,+)}}(x,b)\ =\ (x-r_{1})(x-r_{3})p_{1}(x,b)

(188f)

\displaystyle f_{{}_{(-,-,-)}}(x,b)\ =\ (x-r_{1})(x-r_{2})p_{2}(x,-b)

(188g)

where the roots of the monomials appearing in the above equations read

\displaystyle r_{1}=\frac{(5-b)(N+1)}{2N}\ \ ;\ \ \ \ r_{2}=3\frac{N+1}{N}\ \ ;\ \ \ \ r_{3}=\frac{(5+b)(N+1)}{2N}\ ,

(189)

and the polynomials
p_{1}(x,b),\,p_{2}(x,b),\,p_{3}(x,b)
(of degree 4, 4, 6 respectively) are given explicitly in Appendix
D
.

A few observations on the sADM characteristic polynomial and spectrum are in order:

•

Since
p_{1}(x,b)
and
p_{3}(x,b)
are even in
b
, and
r_{1}(-b)=r_{3}(b)
, the polynomials
f_{\lambda}(x,b)
are simply related to each other under
b\leftrightarrow-b
. Namely, under this symmetry (
188b
) and (
188d
) are exchanged, as well as (
188e
) and (
188g
), and (
188a
), (
188c
), (
188f
) are invariant. This can be easily understood from quantum numbers. Indeed, from (
180
) we see that
b\leftrightarrow-b
is formally equivalent to
T_{t}^{2}\leftrightarrow T_{u}^{2}
, i.e. to the action of the permutation
\sigma_{34}
(see (
184a
)–(
184b
)). We easily verify that under
\sigma_{34}
, the quantum numbers
\lambda=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},\lambda_{3})
are matched to
(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}\lambda_{3},\lambda_{3})
.
30
30

30

This can be seen using
\sigma_{34}=\sigma_{13}\sigma_{14}\sigma_{13}
and the successive transformations of quantum numbers under
\sigma_{13}
and
\sigma_{14}
given in section
5.1
(see paragraph after (
178
)).
Thus, under
\sigma_{34}
, the expression (
188e
) becomes (
188g
). But the same result must be obtained under
b\leftrightarrow-b
. Alternatively, one can use the relation

\displaystyle\sigma_{34}\mathcal{Q}(b)\sigma_{34}=\mathcal{Q}(-b)\ ,

(190)

which is quickly proven by using
T_{t}^{2}=\sigma_{13}T_{s}^{2}\sigma_{13}
,
T_{u}^{2}=\sigma_{14}T_{s}^{2}\sigma_{14}
,
\sigma_{34}\sigma_{14}\sigma_{34}=\sigma_{13}
, and noticing that
\sigma_{34}T_{s}^{2}\sigma_{34}=T_{s}^{2}
.

•

The blocks (of size
>1
) of the sADM corresponding to a given
\lambda
can be further block-diagonalized (as can be seen from (
188a
) and (
188e
)–(
188g
)).

•

The sADM spectrum has a remarkable structure.
Let’s denote by
\mathcal{E}_{+}
the subspace of basis
\mathcal{V}_{{}^{(+,+,+)}}
, and by

\mathcal{E}_{-}
the supplementary subspace (characterized by quantum numbers different from
(+,+,+)
). We observe that the eigenvalues of the sADM restricted to
\mathcal{E}_{-}
, namely
r_{1}
,
r_{2}
,
r_{3}
(each of multiplicity 3) and the 12 eigenvalues given by the roots of the polynomials
p_{1}(x,b)
,
p_{2}(x,b)
and
p_{2}(x,-b)
, are also eigenvalues of the sADM restricted to
\mathcal{E}_{+}
. Since
r_{1}
,
r_{2}
,
r_{3}
have multiplicity 1 in

\mathcal{E}_{+}
, there are six sADM eigenvalues which are ‘endemic’ to this subspace, given by the roots of
p_{3}(x,b)
.

•

An inspection of the polynomials
p_{1}(x,b)
,
p_{2}(x,b)
and
p_{3}(x,b)
(given in Appendix
D
) shows that the set of sADM eigenvalues for the
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
process does not exhibit any
b\leftrightarrow 1/N
symmetry, contrary to the processes
gg\rightarrow gg
(as was observed in
[
14
]
for some subset of the sADM eigenvalues), and
qq\rightarrow qq
(as can be easily verified for the two eigenvalues of the associated sADM, a
2\times 2
matrix in that case).

6
Summary and discussion

In this manuscript, we have studied the color space of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, by explicitly calculating all Hermitian projectors and transition operators associated with
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
. As mentioned in the introduction, the study of this ‘process’ has several motivations (both phenomenological and theoretical) and, to our knowledge, these operators have never been calculated before. Our study shows that with the help of the birdtrack pictorial technique, even non-trivial color calculations can be performed using only elementary tools (e.g. the Fierz identity, color conservation, Schur’s lemma, clebsches).
In particular, our calculations highlight the effectiveness of the quadratic Casimir operator
\hat{C}_{2}
, which acts as a powerful filter of the color space. This is because a given eigenvalue of
\hat{C}_{2}
is shared by only a limited number of irreps of the decomposition of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
(see Table
2
).

When the
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenspace is of dimension 1, the projector on the corresponding irrep is directly obtained from the eigenvector (after proper normalization). As for eigenspaces of dimension
>1
, we have seen that they can be treated simply as follows.

When the eigenspace contains two equivalent irreps, the associated Hermitian projectors and transition operators are given by the
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenvectors having specific symmetries under the
\psi\leftrightarrow\chi
permutation of generalized partons, realized by the operators
\sigma_{12}
and
\sigma_{34}
acting on the initial or final pair. (As mentioned after (
2.2.2
), the fact that any irrep has a specific symmetry under
\psi\leftrightarrow\chi
follows from the requirement that the pair satisfies either Bose-Einstein or Fermi-Dirac statistics.)

In general, an eigenspace of
\hat{C}_{2}
can contain more than two equivalent irreps. In our study, this situation was encountered for the eigenvalue
C_{R}=C_{27}=2(N+1)
, corresponding to three equivalent irreps, one of which is antisymmetric and the other two symmetric. Since the two symmetric irreps cannot be distinguished by the
\psi\leftrightarrow\chi
symmetry, their associated projectors are not uniquely defined – only their sum is. To handle the trickier sector of the
27
, we used clebsches, which simplify the derivation of the three projectors and six transition operators in this sector.

Finally, when the
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenspace contains some irreps which are complex conjugate to each other, those can be distinguished by selecting the eigenvectors which are even and odd under complex conjugation, and finding the precise linear combination of them having the proper symmetry (under permutation of quark/antiquark indices) characterizing the irrep and its complex conjugate.

The particular process we have considered,
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, exhausts all possible reasons for having a degenerate
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenvalue, namely the presence of two complex conjugate irreps and/or two (or more) equivalent irreps. (Note that a
\hat{C}_{2}
eigenspace can contain equivalent irreps as well as their complex conjugates, as is the case for the sector of the
35
discussed in section
4.5
.)
So it seems clear that the procedure we have used to derive the complete color space, based on knowledge of the quadratic Casimir operator (which can be obtained in an elementary way using the Fierz identity), could be automated and applied to more complicated cases. Given its remarkable filtering power, the quadratic Casimir operator may also be a useful tool to implement in advanced algorithms for calculating Hermitian projectors
[
35
,
36
]
.

In the decomposition of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, we found that the presence of two irreps
27
having the same symmetry under
\psi\leftrightarrow\chi

(named
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}
and
{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}
),
has an interesting consequence. Let us denote by
\mathcal{E}_{P}^{27\otimes 27}
the vector space of all
20
self-conjugate projectors and by
\mathcal{E}_{T}^{27\otimes 27}
the supplementary space, consisting of all transition operators and the (non-zero) differences
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!R$}}-{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!\overline{R}$}}
between a projector and its complex conjugate.
We observed that the sum of the two transition operators between
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}
and
{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}
, namely,
({\mathds{T}+\mathds{T}^{\dagger}})_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
, is Hermitian and self-conjugate, and is moreover symmetric under left (
\sigma_{12}
) and right (
\sigma_{34}
) permutations.
Thus, it has the same (
s
-channel) quantum numbers
(\sigma_{\rm cc},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{x})=(+,+,+)

as self-conjugate
projectors.
31
31

31

The quantum numbers were defined with respect to the complex conjugation operator
\sigma_{\rm cc}
and the permutation operators
\sigma_{x}=\sigma_{12}\sigma_{34}
and
\sigma_{y}=\sigma_{14}\sigma_{23}
, the generalized partons being labeled by
1\cdots 4
counterclockwise.

From this, we deduced that the self-conjugate projectors mix with
({\mathds{T}+\mathds{T}^{\dagger}})_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
under crossing symmetry.
In other words, if, for a physics problem involving the color structure of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
, we need to know the (self-conjugate) projectors in the
t
-channel, it is not enough to have previously derived those in the
s
-channel, and one should consider the subspace

\mathcal{E}_{+}=\mathcal{E}_{P}^{27\otimes 27}\oplus\langle{({\mathds{T}+\mathds{T}^{\dagger}})_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}}\rangle
instead of simply
\mathcal{E}_{P}^{27\otimes 27}
.
It should be noted that this situation differs from that encountered for the process
{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}\rightarrow{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}

[
14
]
. In the latter case, the subspace of
s
-channel self-conjugate projectors
\mathcal{E}_{P}^{8\otimes 8}=\langle{\{{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$1$}}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$10$}}+{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{10}$}}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$0$}}$}}\}}\rangle
, and the supplementary subspace
\mathcal{E}_{T}^{8\otimes 8}=\langle{\{{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}_{-}$}},{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}_{-}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$8$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$10$}}$}}-{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$\overline{10}$}}$}}\}}\rangle
, are separately invariant under crossing symmetry.

To give an example of a simple observable where the aforementioned mixing between self-conjugate projectors and
({\mathds{T}+\mathds{T}^{\dagger}})_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
would be at work, let’s consider the
p_{\perp}
-broadening of an energetic
\psi\chi
pair of generalized partons (each being a two-gluon state in the
27
) passing through a nucleus. Similarly to Ref.
[
20
]
, this observable involves (time-ordered) products of diagrams of this type:

(191)

where a dashed line denotes the irrep
27
(see (
6
)), the upper (resp. lower) half of the diagram belongs to the rescattering amplitude (resp. conjugate amplitude), and at each time of the evolution the overall
\psi_{1}\chi_{2}\bar{\chi}_{3}\bar{\psi}_{4}
system is in a color-singlet (quadrupole) state.
32
32

32

This follows from the standard assumption that the rescattering is instantaneous. Here, for the sake of simplicity, the rescattering in (
191
) is also treated in the ‘two-gluon approximation’, where the exchange can be either a
real
(one gluon is exchanged with a target nucleon in both the amplitude and its conjugate), or
virtual
(two gluons are exchanged in the amplitude and none in its conjugate, or vice versa) contribution to the scattering cross section. The specific diagram in (
191
) is a ‘real’ contribution.

The generic diagram (
191
) corresponds to a contribution to
p_{\perp}
-broadening where the
\psi\chi
pair is in the irrep
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}
before rescattering (i.e., projected on
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}
in both the amplitude and conjugate amplitude), and in a
mixed state
after rescattering (
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}
in the amplitude, and
{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}
in the conjugate amplitude).
The particular contribution (
191
) is thus expressed in terms of the antisymmetric clebsch
c_{a}
and symmetric clebsches
c_{1}
and
c_{2}
(defined explicitly in section
4.6.2
), using the pictorial notation
(
83
).

To evaluate (
191
), we first express the
s
-channel projector
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!\alpha$}}
(with
\alpha={\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{-}
) appearing in the left rectangle in terms of
t
-channel operators
\mathcal{V}^{(t)}_{\gamma}
using the matrix
K_{st}=K_{ts}^{-1}
, see (
178a
). (The index
\gamma
runs from 1 to 21, due to the block structure of
K_{st}
.) The gluon exchange, being equivalent to the action of
\frac{1}{2}T_{t}^{2}
(see (
184a
)),
then provides a factor
\frac{1}{2}C_{\gamma}
. Finally, the operator
\mathcal{V}^{(t)}_{\gamma}
is expressed in terms of
s
-channel operators
\mathcal{V}^{(s)}_{\delta}
using the matrix
K_{ts}
. The remaining birdtrack involves only
s
-channel operators, and is non-zero only if
\mathcal{V}^{(s)}_{\delta}=({\mathds{T}+\mathds{T}^{\dagger}})_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
(i.e., if
\delta=21
, see the ordering of the components of
\mathcal{V}^{(s)}
in (
171
)). The transition operator
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\rightarrow{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{+}$}}=c_{2}^{\dagger}c_{1}
(see (
165a
)) appearing in the right rectangle of (
191
) is normalized according to (
85
), and the result for (
191
) reads:

\displaystyle{K}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}$}}\sum_{\gamma=1}^{21}(K_{st})_{\alpha\gamma}\,\frac{C_{\gamma}}{2}\,(K_{ts})_{\gamma\delta}\ \neq 0\ .

(192)

The latter expression shows that (
191
) can only be non-zero if
K_{st}
mixes
({\mathds{T}+\mathds{T}^{\dagger}})_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
with self-conjugate projectors, and the fact that it is indeed non-zero can be checked explicitly from knowledge of the
21\times 21
block
B
in (
5.1
). This illustrates that
p_{\perp}
-broadening can be sensitive to the mixing of
\mathcal{E}_{P}^{27\otimes 27}
and
{\mathds{T}}_{\mbox{${\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}\rightarrow{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{+}$}}
under crossing symmetry.

Finally, let us emphasize that in principle, the elementary method used in our study makes it possible to trace the
N
dependence in the calculation (contained, for example, in Casimir charges and irreps dimensions), as well as the rather complex color structure of certain results. In particular, we could obtain the soft anomalous dimension matrix (sADM) of
{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\to{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}\otimes{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}
almost effortlessly, due to the simple transformation of the chosen basis tensors under crossing symmetry. Indeed, the 42 tensors of the basis
{\cal T}
form a representation of the symmetric group
{\rm S}_{4}
, as can be seen from the simple action of all permutation operators
\sigma_{ij}
in this basis (see Table
4
). We have seen that the organization of basis tensors in subsets of different ‘quantum numbers’, defined as eigenvalues of
\sigma_{x}=\sigma_{12}\sigma_{34}
and
\sigma_{y}=\sigma_{14}\sigma_{23}
(which operators form, together with
\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}=\sigma_{13}\sigma_{24}
and the identity, an abelian subgroup of
{\rm S}_{4}
, the so-called Klein group), explains the main
(21,1,1,1,6,6,6)
block structure of the sADM.
We also observed that these blocks have several eigenvalues in common. We don’t know if there is a simple reason for this, but it is plausible that the
S_{4}
symmetry of the problem has something to do with it.

33

) gives the dimension of the irrep,

.

Appendix C
Non-unicity of
({\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
,
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}})

C.1
Set of solutions

Here we solve the system of equations (
161
) and (
162
) for the coefficients
a,\,b,\,a^{\prime},\,b^{\prime}
entering the expressions (
158
) of the projectors
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}
and
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}
.

Using the change of variables:

\displaystyle\left(\begin{matrix}a\\[5.69054pt]
b\end{matrix}\right)=U_{\theta}\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}X\\[5.69054pt]
Y\end{matrix}\right)\ \ ;\ \ \left(\begin{matrix}a^{\prime}\\[5.69054pt]
b^{\prime}\end{matrix}\right)=U_{\theta}\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}X^{\prime}\\[5.69054pt]
Y^{\prime}\end{matrix}\right)\ \ ;\ \ U_{\theta}\equiv\frac{1}{\sin{2\theta}}\left(\begin{matrix}\ \cos{\theta}\ &\ \sin{\theta}\ \\[5.69054pt]
\ \cos{\theta}\ &\ -\sin{\theta}\ \end{matrix}\right)\ ,

(195)

where the angle
\theta\in\ ]0,\frac{\pi}{4}[
is a fixed parameter defined by

\displaystyle\cos{2\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}\ \ ;\ \ \sin{2\theta}=\sqrt{\frac{\rho-1}{\rho}}\ ,

(196)

the system of equations (
161
)-(
162
) becomes:

\displaystyle X^{2}+Y^{2}\ =\ X^{\prime\,2}+Y^{\prime\,2}\ =\ 1\ \ ;\ \ XX^{\prime}+YY^{\prime}\ =\ 0\ .

(197)

This has an obvious solution:
34
34

34

The other solution obtained by multiplying
X^{\prime}
and
Y^{\prime}
by
-1
changes the sign of
a^{\prime}
and
b^{\prime}
(see (
195
)). This leads to the same projector (
158b
), and to an irrelevant sign change in the transition operators involving the irrep
{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}
. We can thus fix the sign of
X^{\prime}
and
Y^{\prime}
as in (
198
).

\displaystyle X=\cos{t}\ \ ;\ \ Y=-\sin{t}\ \ ;\ \ X^{\prime}=\sin{t}\ \ ;\ \ Y^{\prime}=\cos{t}\ ,

(198)

with
t\in[0,2\pi[
an arbitrary parameter.
Inserting (
198
) into (
195
) we get:

\displaystyle a(t)=\frac{\cos{(t+\theta)}}{\sin{2\theta}}\,;\ b(t)=\frac{\cos{(t-\theta)}}{\sin{2\theta}}\,;\ a^{\prime}(t)=\frac{\sin{(t+\theta)}}{\sin{2\theta}}\,;\ b^{\prime}(t)=\frac{\sin{(t-\theta)}}{\sin{2\theta}}\ ,

(199)

where the
t
-dependence of
a,\,b,\,a^{\prime},\,b^{\prime}
is made explicit. Using (
199
) in (
158
) leads to the expressions (
163
) of the projectors, parametrized by the continuous parameter
t
.

Let us emphasize that the solution (
199
) for a parameter
t
is related to the solution for
t=0
as:

\displaystyle\left(\begin{matrix}a(t)\\[5.69054pt]
a^{\prime}(t)\end{matrix}\right)=R(t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}a(0)\\[5.69054pt]
a^{\prime}(0)\end{matrix}\right)\,;\ \left(\begin{matrix}b(t)\\[5.69054pt]
b^{\prime}(t)\end{matrix}\right)=R(t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}b(0)\\[5.69054pt]
b^{\prime}(0)\end{matrix}\right)\ ,

(200a)

\displaystyle\hskip 71.13188ptR(t)\equiv\left(\begin{matrix}\cos{t}\ &\ -\sin{t}\ \\[5.69054pt]
\sin{t}\ &\ \ \cos{t}\end{matrix}\right)\,.

(200b)

It follows directly that the clebsches (
157
) for a parameter
t
and for
t=0
are related in the same way:

\displaystyle\left(\begin{matrix}c_{1}(t)\\[5.69054pt]
c_{2}(t)\end{matrix}\right)=R(t)\cdot\left(\begin{matrix}c_{1}(0)\\[5.69054pt]
c_{2}(0)\end{matrix}\right)\ .

(201)

C.2
A few possible choices for
({\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}},{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}})

We list below some possible choices for the pair of projectors (
163
), corresponding to simple values of the parameter
t
. Recall that the sum of projectors
{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\rm sum}$}}{}
is given by (
164
).

(a)
t=0

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{1}{2(\sqrt{\rho}-1)}\left[\sqrt{\rho}\left(\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}+\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\right)-\frac{\tilde{Z}}{2n_{12}}\right]\ ,

(202a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{1}{2(\sqrt{\rho}+1)}\left[\sqrt{\rho}\left(\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}+\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\right)+\frac{\tilde{Z}}{2n_{12}}\right]\ .

(202b)

(b)
t=\theta

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{1}{\rho-1}\,\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}+\frac{\rho}{\rho-1}\,\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}+\frac{1}{1-\rho}\,\frac{\tilde{Z}}{2n_{12}}\ ,

(203a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}\ .

(203b)

(c)
t=\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\ ,

(204a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{\rho}{\rho-1}\,\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}+\frac{1}{\rho-1}\,\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}+\frac{1}{1-\rho}\,\frac{\tilde{Z}}{2n_{12}}\ .

(204b)

(d)

t=\frac{\pi}{4}

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27$}}_{+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{1}{2}\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\rm sum}$}}{}-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\rho}{\rho-1}}\left(\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}-\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\right)\ ,

(205a)

\displaystyle{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\mbox{\boldmath$27^{\prime}$}}_{\!\!+}$}}\,=

\displaystyle\ \frac{1}{2}\,{\mathds{P}}_{\mbox{$\!{\rm sum}$}}{}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\rho}{\rho-1}}\left(\frac{\tilde{H}}{n_{11}}-\frac{\tilde{C}}{2(n_{22}+n_{23})}\right)\ .

(205b)

,

appearing as factors in the full characteristic polynomial of the sADM, see (

)–(

).

\displaystyle p_{1}(x,b)\

\displaystyle=\ x^{4}-\frac{x^{3}}{{N}}(9{N}+8)-\frac{x^{2}}{{N}^{2}}(b^{2}{N}^{2}+2b^{2}{N}+7b^{2}-30{N}^{2}-52{N}-19)

\displaystyle+\frac{x}{{N}^{3}}(5b^{2}{N}^{3}+16b^{2}{N}^{2}+31b^{2}{N}+12b^{2}-44{N}^{3}-112{N}^{2}-79{N}-12)

\displaystyle p_{2}(x,b)\

\displaystyle+\frac{x^{2}}{4{N}^{2}}(5b^{2}{N}^{2}+10b^{2}{N}-28b^{2}+86b{N}^{2}+220b{N}+128b+197{N}^{2}+410{N}+204)

\displaystyle+\frac{x}{8{N}^{3}}(5b^{3}{N}^{3}+48b^{3}{N}^{2}+216b^{3}{N}+224b^{3}-51b^{2}{N}^{3}-112b^{2}{N}^{2}+272b^{2}{N}+320b^{2}

\displaystyle\phantom{+\frac{x}{8{N}^{3}}(}-489b{N}^{3}-1712b{N}^{2}-1848b{N}-608b-745{N}^{3}-2320{N}^{2}-2288{N}-704)

\displaystyle\phantom{+\frac{1}{8{N}^{4}}(}+460b{N}^{4}+2036b{N}^{3}+3120b{N}^{2}+1920b{N}+384b+525{N}^{4}+2175{N}^{3}

\displaystyle\phantom{+\frac{1}{8{N}^{4}}(}+3186{N}^{2}+1920{N}+384)\ ,

\displaystyle=\ x^{6}-x^{5}\frac{16({N}+1)}{{N}}-\frac{x^{4}}{{N}^{2}}(5b^{2}{N}^{2}+16b^{2}{N}+47b^{2}-105{N}^{2}-208{N}-91)
